rubrics.justification: Mostly reasonable description of an expanded blastocyst with favorable TE/ICM, but it introduces uncertainty and some inconsistent claims about early hatching/partial hatching versus no hatching, and overinterprets features not clearly verifiable from a single image.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, first cycle status, male factor, sperm parameters, and fresh transfer context well, though endometrial data are missing and some interactions are discussed somewhat generically.

Overall logic is understandable, but there are internal inconsistencies such as suggesting partial hatching and then stating no apparent hatching, and some probability framing is repetitive and not fully tightly linked to the image findings.

Generally consistent with Gardner grading concepts, single embryo transfer for a good-prognosis 34-year-old, avoidance of unproven add-ons, and cautious use of PGT-A; minor deviations include some imprecise staging language and speculative fresh-vs-frozen penalty.

Provides practical next steps including proceeding with single embryo transfer, checking uterine/endometrial optimization, standard luteal support, lifestyle guidance, and a reasonable stepwise plan if unsuccessful.
